policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 16:1 'unto the disciples' carries no possessive; the added αὐτοῦ would give 'his disciples'.
ASV 16:2 'thou canst be no longer steward' renders a present; the future δυνήσῃ would give 'thou shalt not be able'.
ASV 'when I am put out of the stewardship' suits μετασταθῶ with or without ἐκ; the compound verb alone yields 'out of'.
ASV 'their houses' renders ἑαυτῶν and αὐτῶν alike; English does not mark the reflexive here.
ASV 'And he said' is the ASV's rendering of both ὁ δὲ εἶπεν and καὶ εἶπεν; no note is mapped here.
The ASV note on 'bond' reads 'Greek writings', a plural gloss matching τὰ γράμματα against the singular τὸ γράμμα.
ASV 16:7 'He saith unto him, Take thy bond' is asyndetic; the added καὶ would give 'And he saith unto him'.
The ASV note on 'bond' reads 'Greek writings', a plural gloss matching τὰ γράμματα against the singular τὸ γράμμα.
Word order only; ASV 'Make to yourselves friends' does not preserve the Greek order of ἑαυτοῖς and ποιήσατε.
ASV 'when it shall fail' is third person singular; ἐκλίπητε would give 'when ye fail'.
ASV text reads 'that which is your own' (ὑμέτερον) and its textual_variant note puts 'our own' (ἡμέτερον) in the margin as some ancient authorities.
Word order only; ASV 'who will give you' renders δώσει ὑμῖν and ὑμῖν δώσει identically. The verse's textual note concerns ὑμέτερον/ἡμέτερον, not this unit.
ASV 'heard all these things; and they scoffed at him' shows one connective, which the base καὶ before ἐξεμυκτήριζον already supplies; an additional καὶ at πάντα is not distinguished in English.
ASV 'until John' renders μέχρι and ἕως alike; the only note here is an alternative_rendering on 'gospel'.
ASV's second clause is 'and he that marrieth one that is put away', without the 'every one' it gives πᾶς in the first clause.
ASV 16:20 has a single finite verb, 'a certain beggar ... was laid at his gate'; the added ἦν would give 'there was a certain beggar'.
ASV 'named Lazarus was laid at his gate' has no relative clause; the added ὃς would give 'who was laid'.
ASV 16:21 reads 'to be fed with the crumbs that fell', and 'crumbs' renders τῶν ψιχίων, which the base text lacks.
ASV 'licked his sores' renders ἐπέλειχον and ἀπέλειχον alike; the prefix is not distinguished in English.
The article with the proper name Ἀβραάμ has no English reflex; ASV reads 'seeth Abraham afar off' either way.
ASV must supply 'thou' for the second person verb ἀπέλαβες regardless; the emphatic σὺ is not separately marked.
ASV 'And besides all this' fits ἐν and ἐπὶ πᾶσι τούτοις alike; the mapped note is classed alternative_rendering and cannot decide a reading.
ASV 'and that none may cross over from thence to us' does not mark a subject article; μηδὲ with or without οἱ yields the same English.
Word order only; ASV 'I pray thee therefore' renders σε οὖν and οὖν σε identically.
ASV 'But Abraham saith' has the connective δὲ and no indirect object; both r01 and r02 add αὐτῷ, which the ASV would render 'unto him'.
